title: TranscribeIt transcript contract v1
description: FROZEN CONTRACT. Produced by Track A (engine). Consumed by Track B (renderer). All times are seconds as floating point, measured from the start of the source media. Do not change field names or semantics without bumping schemaVersion.

path.description: Absolute path to the original media file the user right-clicked.

fileName.description: Leaf name including extension, for display.

language.description: BCP-47-ish code Whisper detected or was told, e.g. 'en'.

speakerCountMode.description: 'fixed' when the user supplied a speaker count.

elapsedSeconds.description: Total wall-clock for the whole pipeline.

realTimeFactor.description: durationSeconds / elapsedSeconds. >1 means faster than realtime.

speakers.description: One entry per distinct speaker found. Order is by first appearance, so Speaker 1 is whoever spoke first.

label.description: Display-ready label the renderer prints verbatim, e.g. 'Speaker 1'. The renderer must NOT derive its own labels.

turns.description: Contiguous single-speaker passages, sorted ascending by start. Adjacent turns never overlap.

speaker.description: MUST reference an id declared in speakers[]. There is deliberately no sentinel for an unknown speaker: if diarization cannot attribute a passage confidently, assign it to the most likely speaker and set speakerUncertain=true rather than inventing an id. Consumers should still degrade gracefully if handed an unlisted id.

speakerLabel.description: Denormalised copy of speakers[].label so the renderer needs no lookup.

text.description: Whitespace-normalised, leading/trailing trimmed. May contain punctuation from Whisper. Producers MUST NOT emit a turn whose text is empty or whitespace-only - drop the turn instead, because it renders as a bare speaker label with nothing after it. Consumers should nonetheless tolerate one without crashing.

confidence.description: Mean word confidence, or null if unavailable.

speakerUncertain.description: True when diarization overlap was ambiguous. Renderer MAY mark these visually.

words.description: Word-level timings. May be empty if token timings were unavailable, so the renderer must not depend on it.

warnings.description: Human-readable non-fatal issues. The renderer SHOULD surface these in the PDF so the reader knows the transcript's limits.
